subject: Viewing adapted mass matrix in Rstan - possible?

messages.author: cf47bbe63da1f3ae
messages.subject: Viewing adapted mass matrix in Rstan - possible?
parts: I've been looking for a way to do this, when I sift through the elements of the returned fit object I can't find anything that corresponds... get_sampler_params and get_adaptation_info both return nothing.

messages.author: 3f37be0cf708d442
messages.subject: Re: Viewing adapted mass matrix in Rstan - possible?
parts:
From what I can see rstan does not save the mass matrix.

When you load the results from a cmdstan run in rstan, 
the diagonal of the inverse of the mass matrix is in the 
string adaptation_info in the stan_args list, which is part of
the stanfit object. As far as I can tell, the string adaptation_info
is not in stanfit@stan_args when you use rstan for sampling.

For example, you get mass matrix for the first chain with
stanfit@stan_args[[1]]$adaptation_info.

To extract the values out of the string:
adaptation_info = stanfit@stan_args[[1]]$adaptation_info
mass_matrix = eval(parse(text=paste0("c(",strsplit(adaptation_info,"\n#")[[1]][3],")")))

The tricky part is matching the right parameter name to the 
right values, especially if one of your parameters is a 
correlation matrix.

Guido

messages.author: cf47bbe63da1f3ae
messages.subject: Re: Viewing adapted mass matrix in Rstan - possible?
parts:
Thanks. Here is the functions / script to return the variances of sampled parameters over the final adaptation step, assuming the parameters in the model are already unconstrained. If the parameters involve constraints the unconstrain_pars method can be used to get parameters to unconstrained space.


get_stan_params <- function(object) {
  stopifnot(is(object, "stanfit"))
  params <- grep("context__.vals_r", fixed = TRUE, value = TRUE,
    x = strsplit(get_cppcode(get_stanmodel(object)), "\n")[[1]])
  params <- sapply(strsplit(params, "\""), FUN = function(x) x[[2]])
  params <- intersect(params, object@model_pars)
  return(params)
}


get_stan_massmat<-function(fit){
 
spars<-get_stan_params(fit)
spars2<-c()
for(pari in spars){
  spars2<-c(spars2,grep(paste0(pari,'['),names(fit@sim$samples[[1]]),fixed=TRUE))
}

massmat<-list()
for(chaini in 1:fit@sim$chains){
  temp<-c()
for(pari in spars2){
  newval<-cov(cbind(fit@sim$samples[[chaini]][[pari]][(fit@sim$warmup - fit@stan_args[[1]]$control$adapt_term_buffer):fit@sim$warmup]))
  names(newval)<-names(fit@sim$samples[[chaini]])[pari]
  temp<-c(temp,newval)
}
  massmat[[chaini]]<-temp
}
return(massmat)
}


massmat<-get_stan_massmat(fit)

matplot(matrix(log(unlist(massmat)),ncol=length(massmat)),pch=1)

massmat[[1]][massmat[[1]]<.01]

messages.subject: Re: Viewing adapted mass matrix in Rstan - possible?
parts:
Thanks for posting the script!
  
One thing I am wondering about: Doesn't 
this script generally calculate the standard 
deviation of the constrained parameters?
I think that if the model has constrained 
parameters, one would need the standard 
deviation in the unconstrained space when
trying to detect large differences in scale
(or small scales).

The unconstrain_pars method can be used
to get parameters to unconstrained space.
